I bought ten shares of Doge, and the order vanished from my screen. This is Day One. The book showed zero open orders. My screen still said ten. I refreshed the account, then wired the fills into a receipt. There it is. Ten out of ten, with the price I actually paid.

Doge is up. This is Day Two. Did I pick a winner, or did the whole market move? The old index couldn't tell me. I took each active meme's price change, gave them equal weight, then replayed the basket. Now Doge has a benchmark to beat.

Ten shares and a hundred shares have different prices. This is Day Three. I priced a hundred at the first ask. Wrong. There weren't a hundred shares there. I added up the book level by level, then ran the order through the preview. Watch the last share cost more than the first.

That green line is the midpoint. This is Day Four. I thought my buy should fill when the line hit my limit. Wrong line. I added the seller's ask, then drew my resting order beside it. Now I can see the gap my buy still needs to cross.

I left a limit order in the book. This is Day Five. I tried to replace it with more shares than I could afford. Rejected. Losing the original bid here would be brutal. I saved its reservation, then restored it when the edit failed. Same bid. Same queue position.

The exchange runs on a clock, but I can replay it. This is Day Six. A late clock update left a hole in the chart. I collected every tick in the batch, then checked the timestamps. Five seconds at ten ticks a second. Fifty samples, right where they belong.

Seven days ago I was trying to figure out where my Doge order went. This is Day Seven. Today I'm checking the signup form. A typo gets caught. Sending the same address twice should still give me one signup. I checked the email validation, then the duplicate guard. The local form is ready for launch.
